statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail 20 sits at the bottom of the watch band, above the EA_ON range but well below the block threshold, while Stress 49 is elevated and Confidence 87 is high.
recommendation: The deterministic mapping from Tail 20 produces WATCH with a yellow status, pause false and caution true. A narrow danger window is marked from 13:30Z to 14:30Z, spanning the US cash open and the 14:00Z cluster of three medium-impact releases. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: NQ's 60-point pullback fails inside the hour: a fresh extreme at 29,343.00 with price holding 29,328.75, up 0.76%, restores the extension sequence and lifts Tail to 20, mapping to WATCH
body:
The observation that changes this hour reverses the previous one. An hour ago the sixth overnight extreme at 29,290.25 had failed to hold and NQ had retraced about 60 points to 29,228.75, which was read as the first meaningful pullback of the sequence and took Tail down to 15. That pullback has now failed. Barchart shows the September contract at 29,328.75, up 223.00 points or 0.76% on the 29,105.75 settle, with a fresh session high at 29,343.00; Investing.com independently showed 29,304.50, up 0.68%, with a 29,326.00 high on an 08:59Z stamp. Price is holding roughly 14 points, or 0.05%, below the extreme. A shallow retracement that fails within the hour, followed by a new high that price then holds, is precisely the structure the calibration treats as meaningful mean-reversion-failure evidence, and it is the third such element in this sequence alongside repeated extension and NQ sitting near session extremes. Tail rises from 15 to 20, which maps to WATCH.

What keeps this from going further is the absence of independent amplifiers. VIX is 14.89, down 6.00% from Monday's 15.84 close, so volatility is not confirming. Treasury yields have eased rather than aligned: 2Y 4.23%, 5Y 4.39%, 10Y 4.69% down about two basis points, 30Y 5.21%. Crude has extended its decline for a second session, with WTI at $82.61, down 2.82%, and Brent at $89.69, down 2.69%, even as the US rolled out its global sanctions programme focused on Iran and signalled that China would not be exempt. Reporting attributes the fall partly to Middle Eastern flows circumventing the Strait of Hormuz blockade through a protected corridor. Falling oil into an escalatory headline removes an energy-shock premium rather than adding one, so the geopolitical channel is currently a Stress input, not a Tail amplifier.

Breadth is narrow rather than broad, which is the other reason Tail stays at the bottom of the watch band. Delayed latest-session context shows semiconductors positive across all seven tracked names with a mean of about +1.9%, and Technology the strongest sector at +1.02%, but megacaps only six of eight positive with AAPL at -0.11% and MSFT at -0.16%. Index futures show the same tech skew, with NQ around +0.73% against ES +0.37% and YM +0.30%. That is a rotation into the semiconductor complex ahead of the Nvidia report rather than a broad index impulse. Options are pricing a 5.4% Nvidia move, below the 6.5% implied before the May report, so the positioning is directional but not panicked. The whole overnight band, 29,017.00 to 29,343.00, is about 1.12%, which is a persistent drift rather than a violent repricing.

Stress rises to 49 because the failed retracement removes the mean-reversion relief priced an hour ago while the afternoon calendar remains dense: Barkin at 12:00Z, weekly ADP at 12:15Z, Case-Shiller at 13:00Z, the cash open at 13:30Z and three medium-impact releases together at 14:00Z. Confidence is 87, marginally below the previous hour because the two live price feeds disagree on level and session range even though both confirm the new extreme; against that, yields, crude and the shared cross-asset context were all refreshed within minutes of this assessment. The forecast carries the raised level into the cash-open window, peaking at 22 at 14:00Z, and then decays on the assumption that price discovery there is orderly. The dominant catalysts sit just beyond the horizon: Core PCE, the second GDP estimate and Durable Goods at 12:30Z on 26 August, with Nvidia reporting after that session's close.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock-hours carry a published Claude assessment. The window opened at 09:00Z on 24 August with Tail 12 and Stress 50 in a mixed mode and held an 11 to 13 band through the European session. The only non-green slots surrounded the US cash open: Tail 20 with Stress 54 in an event/whipsaw mode at 13:00Z, mapping to WATCH, and the peak at 14:00Z, which reached Tail 26 with Stress 60 in a trend-down mode and mapped to BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES. That episode resolved within a single hour, falling to 13 by 15:00Z and to a floor of 7 by 21:00Z, which is the decay the calibration expects when an event repricing is orderly. The overnight hours ran 8 to 12 in mixed and normal modes until 04:00Z, when the mode turned to trend-up and Tail climbed through 13, 14 and 15 to 17 at 07:00Z as successive higher extremes accumulated, before easing to 15 at 08:00Z on a retracement that has since failed. Stress spent the whole window between 42 and 60 and Confidence between 80 and 88, so evidence quality was never the constraint.
outlookSummary: The conditional path opens at Tail 20 on the observed failure of the 60-point pullback and a fresh extreme at 29,343.00, which maps this hour to WATCH. It eases to 19 and then 18 through the quiet European stretch on the assumption that an unconfirmed one-way sequence ages, holds 18 across the Barkin and weekly ADP checkpoints, then rebuilds to 20 at 13:00Z as Case-Shiller prints and the cash open follows at 13:30Z. The peak is 22 at 14:00Z, where three medium-impact releases land inside the first half hour of cash trade at the centre of the 13:30Z to 14:30Z danger window, and 15:00Z is still 20 while the opening auction resolves. Four slots therefore map to WATCH and the remaining twenty to EA_ON. The series then decays through 18, 17 and 16 across the afternoon, steps back to 17 at 20:00Z where the cash close overlaps a second Barkin appearance, and falls to an 11 floor in the thin pre-Asia hours. The final stretch rebuilds gently from 11 to 16 as Asia opens and Europe approaches Core PCE day, on calendar structure rather than observed price path. Stress follows the same shape between 40 and 56, and Confidence decays from 87 to 62 purely as a function of evidence age.
